title: Design the to-be onboarding process
scenario:
Today: the seller uploads documents → waits ~8 days → a KYC reviewer checks everything by hand → if anything is wrong, the seller gets an email, re-uploads **all** documents and waits again → after approval the catalogue team sets up the first listing (~3 days).

The approved changes are: automatic **document readability check** at upload, **penny-drop bank verification** (deposit ₹1 and read back the account holder name), **GSTIN auto-validation**, a **48-hour SLA** for manual KYC review, **WhatsApp status updates**, and **re-upload of only the failed document**.

> "Show me the new flow on one page, so ops, engineering and the KYC team agree on who does what."
task:
Draw the **to-be** process as a Mermaid flowchart. Include:

- the seller's **upload** with the **automatic checks** (readability, penny-drop bank check, GSTIN) and what happens when each fails
- **manual KYC review** with its **48-hour SLA**
- **approve** and **reject** paths, with **re-upload of the failed document only**
- **WhatsApp** notifications at key status changes
- the end state: seller **live**

Use subgraphs (lanes) for at least two actors, e.g. `subgraph Seller` and `subgraph KYC team`.
hints: Lanes in Mermaid: `subgraph S[Seller] ... end`. Nodes can link across subgraphs.
Automatic checks are decisions: `C1{Readable?} -->|No| U[Retake photo]`, which loops back to upload *before* submission. That's the whole point.

Show where the SLA applies: `K[Manual KYC review
SLA 48 h]`.
Rejection should loop to re-uploading **the failed document only**, not the whole application.
explanation:
A to-be map is judged on whether it **removes the pain points** found in the as-is:

- **Shift-left validation**: readability, bank name and GSTIN are checked *at upload*, so most bad submissions never reach the KYC queue (they caused ~77% of rejections).
- **Shorter loops**: a rejected seller re-uploads one document instead of restarting.
- **Visible SLAs**: the 48-hour review target sits on the manual step, so it can be measured.
- **Proactive communication**: WhatsApp updates replace "call support to ask".
- **Lanes make ownership explicit**, which is what lets ops, engineering and KYC agree.

Compare with the example. Your layout can differ; check that every approved change appears and every decision has labelled exits.
interview:
*"After mapping the as-is seller onboarding, I designed the to-be flow with swimlanes for seller, system and KYC team, moving document, bank and GSTIN checks to the point of upload and adding a 48-hour SLA on manual review. Walking ops and engineering through one diagram got sign-off in a single meeting."*

Expect: **"How would you measure whether the to-be process works?"** % live within 10 days, first-time-right rate, KYC queue age and status calls per week.

rubric: Automatic checks happen before submission, with a loop back on failure
Manual KYC review shows the 48-hour SLA
Rejection loops to re-uploading only the failed document
WhatsApp updates appear at key status changes
At least two lanes (subgraphs) show who does each step
